correctness.rationale: On the sum-zero hyperplane in characteristic two, splitting off the all-ones vector makes the cubic independent of the vertex coordinate. The gradient on the hyperplane vanishes precisely where all coordinates have equal squares, giving the sole geometric singular point; the five-coordinate slice is smooth since five is odd. In an affine chart at the vertex the initial and full local equation is the nonzero homogeneous cubic, so its multiplicity is three. A plane avoiding the vertex would project injectively to a plane in the smooth cubic surface, impossible; planes through the vertex biject with the 27 lines. The 15 pairings give distinct surviving planes (the allowed equalities identify exactly the paired coordinate functionals). Independent exhaustive line enumeration confirms 15 fixed by Frobenius and all 27 fixed by its square. The six-coordinate action on the slice quotient is faithful: a 3-cycle moves a point represented by a vector with two ones, and every nontrivial normal subgroup of S6 contains the 3-cycles. Vikulova's identification then applies. Frobenius squared fixes Picard because the geometric line classes span it; the count 15 over F2 gives trace five in rank seven, hence multiplicities six and one for +1 and -1. Each base point lifts to q nonvertex points, giving the stated formula.
residual_risks: The argument counts geometric planes and does not determine the plane Hilbert scheme or the Jacobian singular scheme. Vertex multiplicity is not the length of the Jacobian scheme. The comparison concerns the defining equations at characteristic zero and two; it does not assume flatness of the unnormalized sum-of-cubes equation at the prime three.
